title: Ghost sightings, phantom battles and eerie legends haunt these landmarks
excerpt: Herefordshire has plenty of haunted spots in the county. Here are five of them to visit for Halloween.
content:
Herefordshire has plenty of haunted spots in the county.

Here are five haunted Herefordshire locations to visit as Halloween approaches next month.

Hellens Manor, Much Marcle

Often described as Herefordshire’s most famous haunted house, Hellens Manor is steeped in centuries of ghost stories.

Its best-known spirit is Hetty Walwyn, a young woman who allegedly eloped against her family’s wishes before being confined to a room in the manor for decades.

Visitors and staff have reported sightings of her ghost wandering the corridors, particularly near the room where she was said to have been imprisoned.

The manor is also linked to an apparition of a Catholic priest reportedly killed there during the English Civil War.

Hampton Court Castle, Hope-under-Dinmore

Not to be confused with the royal palace near London, Hampton Court Castle has long been associated with paranormal activity.

Local legends tell of the Grey Lady, believed to be a heartbroken servant whose spirit is said to drift through the castle’s halls and gardens.

Staff and visitors have reported unexplained whispers, strange scents and mysterious occurrences within the historic building.

The castle is also linked to the legend of the Coningsby Hound painting, which folklore claims should never be removed or misfortune will follow.

Eastnor Castle, near Ledbury

The Gothic Revival Eastnor Castle has developed a reputation for ghostly encounters over the years.

Stories centre on a female spirit believed to be a former resident mourning a lost love.

Witnesses have spoken of unexplained footsteps echoing through empty corridors, doors closing on their own and unusual cold spots.

Its dramatic appearance beneath the Malvern Hills adds to the eerie atmosphere that has made it popular with paranormal enthusiasts.

Wigmore Castle, north Herefordshire

The ruins of medieval Wigmore Castle are among the county’s most atmospheric historic sites and have inspired numerous ghost tales.

Visitors have reported hearing phantom battles, including clashing swords and distant war cries.

Legend also speaks of a spectral knight who patrols the ancient walls before disappearing without a trace.

Its turbulent history and strategic importance along the Welsh Marches have helped make it one of Herefordshire’s enduring paranormal hotspots.

The Green Dragon Hotel, Hereford

One of Hereford’s oldest and most famous buildings, the historic Green Dragon Hotel has attracted ghost stories for generations.

Reports include sightings of a Victorian woman descending the staircase, a phantom bellboy appearing to guests and mysterious noises in empty rooms.

Some visitors have also described sudden cold spots and unexplained feelings of being watched.

The hotel remains one of the city’s best-known allegedly haunted locations.
